Nothing Besides Hashem
"We know Russian!" Yochi giggles.
"Nyet nyet nikavo!"
She and her twin brother Yossi
sing at the top of their lungs,
clickety-clacking their rhythm
sticks as they march around the
dining room table.
"Yes, this is a Russian niggun,"
calls their older sister Sara, who
is talking to Esther Miriam on
the couch. "Did you know that
from the time of the Frierdiker
Rebbe, until just forty years ago,
the Russian government didn’t let
people teach about Hashem?"
"That didn't stop us Chassidim,"
declaresTzvi, putting down his
piccolo as he marches behind
the twins. "We sang proudly—in
Russian—that there is nothing
besides Hashem."
"Yeah!" Sara grins. “We used
their own language to talk about
Hashem—and that’s powerful!
Russia now has
Chabad Houses,
and summer
camps, and shuls
where everyone
can learn how there
really is nothing
besides Hashem."
"That’s a sign that
Moshiach’s mamesh
almost here," says
Tzvi, grinning back.
"Totally geuladik!”
Esther Miriam calls
out, grabbing her
tambourine and
joining the march.

A Home for
Chabad of
Prescott
Nothing seemed to be working
out.Would we ever have a proper
Chabad House?
Our family is on shlichus in Prescott, Arizona.
When our parents first came to Prescott,
they rented a house to live in. Because they
didn’t own a big Chabad House yet, they
hosted programs in the house and in other
places around town.
In 5775 (2015), someone donated a lot of
money—enough to buy a Chabad House!
Tatty and Mommy began searching for just
the right building in just the right spot. A few
months later, they found the perfect building.
Unfortunately, there was a problem.The
owner wanted an enormous amount of
money, a lot more thanTatty and Mommy
could pay.Tatty offered a lower price, but the
owner wouldn’t hear of it.
Tatty asked his friends what to do, but their
answers confused him. “Borrow money from
the bank so you can buy it,” some friends
advised. Others, however, thought differently.
“Don’t go into debt!” they warned, “it’s not
worth it.”
All this back and forth made
Tatty’s head spin. Looking for
some clarity, he sat down to
write a letter to the Rebbe.
I’m confused, he wrote. People
are giving me opposite pieces of
advice. Rebbe, what should I do?
A short while later,Tatty heard
that the owner of the building
was planning to sell it to someone
else. Okay, he thought. It must be
hashgacha pratis that we’re not
meant to buy it.
But in the end, that deal didn’t work out.
The building was put up for sale again.
As soon as he heard this,Tatty wrote another
letter to the Rebbe, this time asking for a
bracha.Then, he called his real estate agent.
“Can you tell the owner that we want to buy it?”
The agent passed on the message, but the
owner didn’t respond.
A month later,Tatty got a letter from the
owners of the house we were renting.When
he opened it up, his heart sank. Your lease is
up in 40 days, the letter said. We don’t want to

Battle Plan
Even now in Golus, Hashem stands with every Yid.
Usually, soldiers are not in the same place as their
commanders. But Hashem is different; He is with
every single chayol at every moment. Like the passuk
says, “יו ָָל ָ
ָע ב ָ

learn, daven, and do mitzvos, and He is ready to bring
the Geulah as soon as our avodah has been completed.
Just like the miracles of Yetzias Mitzrayim were clear
for all to see, the same will happen in our final Geulah.
The entire world will watch as Hashem takes everyYid
out of Golus with open and revealed nissim.
This will start with us chayolim, just like the children
in Mitzrayim recognized Hashem before anyone else.
Let’s keep looking for ways to share our love forTorah
andmitzvosevenbetterthanbefore.Afterall,Hashem
is with us, waiting to perform the biggest miracles yet!

Orders from our General
The first ger tzedek (righteous convert)
mentioned in the Torah isYisro, Moshe’s
father-in-law. Yisro was an important
person living in Midyan, far from the
midbar.Whatmadehimleaveeverything
behind and become aYid?
All the way in Midyan, Yisro heard about
the miracles that Hashem did for the
Yidden during Yetzias Mitzrayim and
KriasYam Suf. He was so impressed that
he decided to join theYidden at Har Sinai.
He wanted to receive the Torah and
become part of this special nation, too.
This shows us that Hashem is always
witheveryYidanddoesopenmiraclesfor
them—so much so, that even someone
as far away asYisro could hear about it!

TheYetzer Hara comes and argues:
You’re only a child—not even bar mitzvah
or bas mitzvah yet!You don’t have to
keep all the mitzvos like an adult.
So why should you learnTorah and
follow its ways now?
Why not spend your time doing the
things that so many other kids love
and are passionate about?
Torah can wait until you are older.
No,Yetzer Hara! You say that
I am too young forTorah—
but you cannot fool me!

At Har Sinai, Hashem gave theTorah
to Moshe Rabbeinu. Moshe passed it
on to every Yid, including me!
I am Hashem’s child and part of Kehillas
Yaakov.Torah is my inheritance.
Yetzer Hara, you know that an
inheritance does not depend on age.
It can even belong to a newborn baby.
I do not have to become older,
smarter, or more learned.
The entireTorah already belongs to me!
And everyone knows that an
inheritance is extra special.
It isn't just valuable—it reminds you
of the person who gave it to you, and
that's what makes it so precious.
My inheritance is from Hashem
Himself—the OneWho created me, loves
me, and gives me everything I have.
And this is no ordinary gift. It is
Hashem’s most precious treasure!
Belongs to you? Fine. But do not pretend
that Torah is really precious to you.
I know what is precious to you—your
games, your toys, and the things you enjoy.
Look what happens when someone takes
your favorite toy without permission.You
become angry and upset. If it gets lost or
broken, it really hurts.
But if someone takes away some of your
Torah-learning time and gives you extra
recess instead, are you upset?
Maybe you are happy!
So what is really precious to you?
You are right about one thing,Yetzer
Hara.The way I treat something shows
how precious it is to me.
But that does not prove that
Torah is not precious. It proves that
you have been trying to make me
forget how precious it really is!
A toy becomes precious because it
belongs to me.Torah belongs to me too—
butTorah is infinitely
more precious than any toy.
Yetzer Hara, of course you do
not want me to learnTorah.

In this series, we will explore arguments
that theYetzer Hara uses against us
and discover how theTwelve Pesukim
guide us to stand strong, answer back,
and win the battle.
THETWELVEPESUKIMPUTTOWORK
10 681
Torah is my guide, my book of orders,
and my battle plan as a soldier in
Hashem’s Army. It teaches me how
to fight you—theYetzer Hara—and
complete the mission Hashem gave me.
You try convincing me to
wait until I am older.
You know how powerful the pure
Torah ofYiddishe children is.
It protects the Jewish people and
destroys the plans of our enemies.
You also want me to forget the value of
Torah and what it can accomplish.
Torah is the master plan Hashem
used to create the world.
When I learnTorah, my mind
connects with Hashem’s wisdom.
When I do a mitzvah, I put Hashem’s
plan into action and help the world
become what it was created to be.
Yetzer Hara, you pretend to be my
friend by making the things that
are popular among other kids seem
more important thanTorah.
But I know what you are really trying to
do: You are trying to make me forget my
treasure, my power, and my mission!
TheTorah belongs to me now.
It gives me the strength to
stand up and fight as a soldier now.
The Jewish people—and the entire world
—need the light of my Torah now.
So,Yetzer Hara, you thought that
by starting this conversation, you’d
convince me to drop theTorah for
games and toys. But you are so wrong.
Now that you’ve challenged me, I’m
going to show you just how much I
loveTorah with all of my heart.
I will take the passion that
I have for my games and toys and
use it instead for Hashem and
HisTorah. Just you wait and see!
I will cherishTorah and learn it
with my whole heart.
I will live by it. I will share it.
I will use its power to defeat you
and help protect the Jewish people.
TheTorah is mine.
Mine for real.

enemy’s strategy.This way, we avoid falling into his trap. In
Tzivos Hashem we face the trickiest enemy: theYetzer Hara.
Here’s his strategy: First, theYetzer Hara plants negative
thoughts in our heads.Then, those thoughts grow into worse
feelings that can lead to even more dangerous actions.

In a war, the first step toward victory is to expose the
enemy’s strategy.This way, we avoid falling into his trap. In
Tzivos Hashem we face the trickiest enemy: theYetzer Hara.
Here’s his strategy: First, theYetzer Hara plants negative
thoughts in our heads.Then, those thoughts grow into worse
feelings that can lead to even more dangerous actions.
expose the enemy
One of the ways theYetzer Hara tricks us is by telling us to be apathetic.This means to be detached
and uncaring about what’s happening around us (different from ‘'pathetic’, which means ‘in a pitiful or
sorry state).TheYetzer Hara’s goal is for us to shut out other people’s feelings and be insensitive. He tries
convincing us that if we think of others, there won’t be any space left to feel our own feelings or properly
care for ourselves.
Look at the following scene and identify where theYetzer Hara could influence you to be apathetic
towards others, and trigger your thoughts, speech, and actions.

A Home for
Chabad of
Prescott
Nothing seemed to be working
out. Would we ever have a proper
Chabad House?
Our family is on shlichus in Prescott, Arizona.
When our parents first came to Prescott,
they rented a house to live in. Because they
didn’t own a big Chabad House yet, they
hosted programs in the house and in other
places around town.
In 5775 (2015), someone donated a lot of
money—enough to buy a Chabad House!
Tatty and Mommy began searching for just

the right building in just the right spot. A few
months later, they found the perfect building.
Unfortunately, there was a problem. The
owner wanted an enormous amount of
money, a lot more than Tatty and Mommy
could pay. Tatty offered a lower price, but the
owner wouldn’t hear of it.
Tatty asked his friends what to do, but their
answers confused him. “Borrow money from
the bank so you can buy it,” some friends
advised. Others, however, thought differently.
“Don’t go into debt!” they warned, “it’s not
worth it.”
All this back and forth made
Tatty’s head spin. Looking for
some clarity, he sat down to
write a letter to the Rebbe.
I’m confused, he wrote. People
are giving me opposite pieces of
advice. Rebbe, what should I do?
A short while later, Tatty heard
that the owner of the building
was planning to sell it to someone
else. Okay, he thought. It must be
hashgacha pratis that we’re not
meant to buy it.
But in the end, that deal didn’t work out.
The building was put up for sale again.
As soon as he heard this, Tatty wrote another
letter to the Rebbe, this time asking for a
bracha. Then, he called his real estate agent.
“Can you tell the owner that we want to buy it?”
The agent passed on the message, but the
owner didn’t respond.
A month later, Tatty got a letter from the
owners of the house we were renting. When
he opened it up, his heart sank. Your lease is
up in 40 days, the letter said. We don’t want to

Change Everything?
Orders from our General
The first ger tzedek (righteous convert)
mentioned in the Torah is Yisro, Moshe’s
father-in-law. Yisro was an important
person living in Midyan, far from the
midbar.What made him leave everything
behind and become a Yid?
All the way in Midyan, Yisro heard about
the miracles that Hashem did for the
Yidden during Yetzias Mitzrayim and
Krias Yam Suf. He was so impressed that
he decided to join the Yidden at Har Sinai.
He wanted to receive the Torah and
become part of this special nation, too.
This shows us that Hashem is always
with every Yid and does open miracles for
them—so much so, that even someone
as far away as Yisro could hear about it!

Battle Plan
Even now in Golus, Hashem stands with every Yid.
Usually, soldiers are not in the same place as their
commanders. But Hashem is different; He is with
every single chayol at every moment. Like the passuk
says, “—”ְוְ ִהִֵנֵ ה ה' ִנִ ָצב ָעָלָ יוHashem watches closely as we
learn, daven, and do mitzvos, and He is ready to bring
the Geulah as soon as our avodah has been completed.
Just like the miracles of Yetzias Mitzrayim were clear
for all to see, the same will happen in our final Geulah.
The entire world will watch as Hashem takes every Yid
out of Golus with open and revealed nissim.
This will start with us chayolim, just like the children
in Mitzrayim recognized Hashem before anyone else.
Let’s keep looking for ways to share our love for Torah
and mitzvos even better than before. After all, Hashem
is with us, waiting to perform the biggest miracles yet!

message. Use the hints to help you, and look at the black
boxes to see where each word begins and ends.

Smooth out the newspaper and
play again!

You’re only a child—not even bar mitzvah
or bas mitzvah yet! You don’t have to
keep all the mitzvos like an adult.
So why should you learn Torah and
follow its ways now?

Belongs to you? Fine. But do not pretend
that Torah is really precious to you.
I know what is precious to you—your
games, your toys, and the things you enjoy.

Look what happens when someone takes
your favorite toy without permission. You
become angry and upset. If it gets lost or
broken, it really hurts.

At Har Sinai, Hashem gave the Torah
to Moshe Rabbeinu. Moshe passed it
on to every Yid, including me!

But if someone takes away some of your
Torah-learning time and gives you extra
recess instead, are you upset?
Maybe you are happy!
So what is really precious to you?

I am Hashem’s child and part of Kehillas
Yaakov. Torah is my inheritance.

You are right about one thing, Yetzer
Hara. The way I treat something shows
how precious it is to me.

Yetzer Hara, you know that an
inheritance does not depend on age.
It can even belong to a newborn baby.
I do not have to become older,
smarter, or more learned.

But that does not prove that
Torah is not precious. It proves that
you have been trying to make me

The entire Torah already belongs to me!

And this is no ordinary gift. It is

Why not spend your time doing the

but you cannot fool me!

My inheritance is from Hashem
Himself—the One Who created me, loves
me, and gives me everything I have.

A toy becomes precious because it
belongs to me. Torah belongs to me too—
but Torah is infinitely
more precious than any toy.
Yetzer Hara, of course you do
not want me to learn Torah.

Torah is my guide, my book of orders,
and my battle plan as a soldier in
Hashem’s Army. It teaches me how
to fight you—the Yetzer Hara—and
complete the mission Hashem gave me.
You try convincing me to
wait until I am older.
You know how powerful the pure
Torah of Yiddishe children is.
It protects the Jewish people and
destroys the plans of our enemies.

But I know what you are really trying to
do: You are trying to make me forget my
treasure, my power, and my mission!
The Torah belongs to me now.
It gives me the strength to
stand up and fight as a soldier now.
The Jewish people—and the entire world
—need the light of my Torah now.
So, Yetzer Hara, you thought that
by starting this conversation, you’d
convince me to drop the Torah for
games and toys. But you are so wrong.

You also want me to forget the value of
Torah and what it can accomplish.

Now that you’ve challenged me, I’m

Torah is the master plan Hashem
used to create the world.

I will take the passion that
I have for my games and toys and
use it instead for Hashem and

When I learn Torah, my mind

When I do a mitzvah, I put Hashem’s

become what it was created to be.
Yetzer Hara, you pretend to be my
friend by making the things that
are popular among other kids seem
more important than Torah.

I will cherish Torah and learn it
with my whole heart.
I will live by it. I will share it.
I will use its power to defeat you
and help protect the Jewish people.
The Torah is mine.
Mine for real.

In a war, the first step toward victory is to expose the
enemy’s strategy. This way, we avoid falling into his trap. In
Tzivos Hashem we face the trickiest enemy: the Yetzer Hara.
Here’s his strategy: First, the Yetzer Hara plants negative
thoughts in our heads. Then, those thoughts grow into worse
feelings that can lead to even more dangerous actions.

One of the ways the Yetzer Hara tricks us is by telling us to be apathetic. This means to be detached
and uncaring about what’s happening around us (different from ‘'pathetic’, which means ‘in a pitiful or
sorry state). The Yetzer Hara’s goal is for us to shut out other people’s feelings and be insensitive. He tries
convincing us that if we think of others, there won’t be any space left to feel our own feelings or properly
care for ourselves.

One time, while Mommy was at aYud Shvat Farbrengen,
the lady sitting next to her said, “I want to share an
amazing story with you.

“For the past few nights, my baby has not been sleeping
well. When we’d put him in bed, he would cry and cry!
So we’d take him out of the crib, calm him
down, and put him back in bed. But a
few minutes later, he would wake
up and start crying again!
We were at our wits’ end, when
my husband noticed that the
Chitas and pushka were
missing from the
baby’s room!

this story—not just because

but because she and Tatty were

me! During the past few nights,
I had been waking up a lot and
wasn’t getting proper sleep.
Mommy and Tatty didn’t know

As soon as she got home, she

the Rebbe wants each of us to
have a Cheder Tzivos Hashem,

keeping a Chitas in the room.
Of course, I happily brought the
Chitas back, and what do you
know—Baruch Hashem, I’m back
to sleeping through the night.
